ANNOTATION_read_this_first.headline: Route B at 3.0 m sub-legs: 2 of 3 segments executed. Sub-leg 1 REACHED TARGET at 0.094 m; sub-leg 2 failed at 0.2594 m on vio_realign_incomplete. The cause was the CONTROL LAW, not BLE.
ANNOTATION_read_this_first.proximate_cause: Sub-leg 2's second realignment, after linear pulse 9, needed a 51.025 deg correction with only 0.2594 m left to run, and the turn was refused `turn_budget_infeasible`. That refusal is what surfaces as `vio_realign_incomplete`. It is the documented geometric inflation of aim error as range closes -- atan(cross_track / distance) grows without bound as distance shrinks -- so a modest cross-track error accumulated over 3.0 m becomes an uncorrectable angle in the last 25 cm.

MY_PREDICTION_WAS_REFUTED.what_I_predicted: From docs/evidence-ble-cadence-predictors-20260821.json (cadence degrades with time into a run; stall fraction 9.1% -> 25%) I predicted sub-leg 2, running later in the session, would degrade on BLE refresh cadence.
MY_PREDICTION_WAS_REFUTED.what_actually_happened: Cadence did NOT degrade. Sub-leg 1 mean cadence 0.85 (min 0.53); sub-leg 2 mean 0.89 (min 0.74) -- slightly BETTER. ZERO stalled pulses (<0.3) in either segment across all 19 linear pulses of a 130.4 s run. Queue depth was 0 and the link live at the moment of failure.
MY_PREDICTION_WAS_REFUTED.what_this_means: The time-into-run cadence trend is a POPULATION tendency across 24 runs, not a within-run law, and it does not predict any individual run. It should not be used to attribute a specific failure. This run is a clean counterexample and is recorded as such.

what_this_run_DOES_establish: A 3.0 m sub-leg CAN reach target: 0.094 m, comfortably inside the 0.15 m tolerance.
Two 3.0 m sub-legs now land on record (0.1484 m on the earlier single-leg run, 0.094 m here).
Route B executed 2 of 3 chained segments -- the furthest a chain has got. Previous end-to-end record was 0 for 2.
The splitter is correct again: 3 sub-legs of 3.000002 m, keep-outs checked (2 zones, 0 violations).
BLE is NOT the binding constraint at 3.0 m over ~130 s -- measured, not assumed.
what_is_still_NOT_established: A full 3-of-3 chain. Sub-leg 3 never ran.
That 3.0 m is reliable: 3.0 m legs are now 2 reached / 1 failed, n=3.
The measured-good regime remains ~0.8 m; 3.0 m is still ~4x outside it.
ANNOTATION_read_this_first.the_real_open_problem: Cross-track accumulation over a long leg, meeting a correction budget that cannot deliver large angles at short range. This is the same failure FAMILY as the 3.85 m run on 2026-08-20 (18 deg opening aim error -> mid-drive correction -> overshoot). ⚠️ Do NOT respond by raising vio_max_realignments: that was tried, reviewed twice and reverted twice. The lever, if any, is reducing cross-track accumulation, or correcting EARLIER while the geometry is still forgiving -- not by allowing more late corrections.
ANNOTATION_read_this_first.procedure: Path frozen from the scan and NOT re-derived: preflight measured 0.000 m drift against the scanned start. Gate armed inside the same try whose finally disarms, then DISARMED and independently verified after (enabled false, real_motion_allowed false).

safety_gates.name: stop_primitive_available
safety_gates.detail: Coordinator must expose async_stop_manual_motion().

safety_gates.name: ble_transport_required
safety_gates.detail: Real closed-loop motion requires the BLE transport for responsive telemetry; cloud/Wi-Fi lag is unsafe for guarded path execution. BLE must also report itself usable -- being selected for routing does not mean a command can be delivered.

safety_gates.name: ble_link_live
safety_gates.detail: Real motion requires a conservative BLE preflight -- a live client, an open dispatch gate, an empty command queue, and a recent outbound attempt. 'Usable' only means BLE is eligible for routing; it stays True while the command queue is gated and commands (including the mandatory stop that bounds a pulse) accumulate undelivered. The send path separately waits for confirmed queue start and GATT-write completion. See docs/pymammotion-ble-slot-leak-bug.md.

safety_gates.name: segment_too_long
safety_gates.detail: Segment length is capped at 6.1 m by authorization, not by a measured reach limit; the longest segment ever executed is 4.0 m.

safety_gates.name: linear_budget_insufficient_for_segment
safety_gates.detail: 22 linear pulses reach about 6.60 m at a stall-tolerant 0.3 m/pulse, short of this segment.
